- Any evidence artifacts you can provide to demonstrate deletion (audit logs, export manifests, CAIQ/SOC2 references).

Subject: Re: Access/Delete request for patient records — controller/processor clarity and timing

Hi Elena — thanks for the heads up and the clear asks. High-level answers first, then proposed timeline and who does what:

Controller vs Processor
- For inference request payloads you submit via our API and the Nightingale account configuration, Nightingale is the data controller. Redwood acts as a processor for request payloads, generated outputs, and short-term runtime logs.
- There are exceptions (e.g., if Nightingale configured retention to persist raw audio/uploads on our storage tier under their control) — please flag any such exceptions.

Verification steps and timeline (proposed)
- Step 1 (initial triage & identity verification): 24–48 hours. We will verify requestor identity against Nightingale-provided proof points.
- Step 2 (access export): Provide a scoped export (user metadata + inference context) within 7 business days. Large retrievals may take up to 10 business days; we'll flag size at triage.
- Step 3 (deletion confirmation): Once deletion is authorized by Nightingale (controller directive), Redwood will initiate irreversible deletion of active inference caches and secondary indexes and will provide an audit manifest within 30 days.

Evidence we can provide
- Audit manifest showing purged object keys and timestamps (attachment stub).
- SOC 2 evidence index and CAIQ pointers to logging controls (we can provide the index PDF and redacted sample logs where allowed).
- Mapping of export schema to storage locations (CSV).

Proposed escalation / contacts
- Primary contact (Redwood privacy ops): karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
- Legal/contract clarifications: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
- If verification stalls past the SLAs above: escalate to jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com (I will coordinate with infra).

I attached an index of the typical artifacts and a mapping CSV for the export layout — please confirm if the export scope below is sufficient, and we'll start triage.

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer — Privacy Integrations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: evidence_index_SOC2_v3.pdf (index of artifacts), export_schema_mapping.csv

Elena / Jordan — looping in a short legal note on controller/processor and escalation obligations:

- Confirming Jordan's summary: Nightingale is controller; Redwood is processor. The DPA (Section 3.2) outlines that controller directives for deletion are binding and Redwood will act on written controller instructions.
- Evidence: we can provide an audit manifest and a deletion manifest; however, full raw logs containing patient pseudonyms may require a mutual redaction plan before transfer due to Nightingale's internal data minimization policy.
- SCCs & DPIA impact: If these requests are part of a DPIA remediation, we recommend updating the SCC Annex to reflect a <30 day deletion confirmation target and adding a short schedule to clarify responsibilities.

Operational ask for Nightingale: please provide the controller directive email including: the subject, list of user ids, and an authorized contact for identity verification. That will start our formal runbook.

I'll prepare a DPA amendment template if you want that pushed to DocuSign after we agree on the timelines.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: verification_checklist_v2.xlsx

Thanks — operational commitments from Redwood privacy ops:

Verification flow:
- Within 48 hours of receiving Nightingale's controller directive + identity proof, we will confirm scoped export size and provide a triage summary.
- For exports <= 5GB: deliver within 5 business days. For exports > 5GB: target 10 business days, with interim status updates every 48 hours.
- Deletion workflow: upon receipt of controller deletion instruction, we will: 1) liquidate active caches (immediate), 2) schedule background retention deletions across object stores (completed within 30 days), 3) provide a signed deletion manifest and SHA256 checksums for exported manifests where applicable.

Escalation matrix (if verification stalls):
- T+48 hours: raise to privacy ops (karthik.iyer@).
- T+72 hours: escalate to legal (marissa.cole@).
- T+5 business days: escalate to Jordan Blake for infra intervention.

SLA exceptions: bulk archival tiers are subject to third-party vendor compaction windows — we'll document any vendor-imposed delays in the triage summary.

I'll queue the requests for NB-54321 and NB-47790 when you send the signed controller directive.

-Karthik
